key_insight: Mean-flow skew changes a turbulent mixing layer mainly in magnitude, reducing mean and turbulent quantities by up to about 40%, but leaves its core self-similar mixing-layer dynamics largely intact.
engineering_relevance: For 3D shear-flow design, this suggests skew can weaken transport without fundamentally changing scaling laws, providing a practical benchmark for predicting free-shear mixing in realistic configurations.
method: Added spanwise mean-flow deflection with turning vanes near a splitter plate trailing edge.
Measured downstream flow evolution using cross-wire anemometry.
Compared planar and skewed cases using similarity scaling, shear-layer thickness growth, Reynolds-stress profiles, and Townsend's structure parameter.
evidence_signal: Experimental results showed systematic reductions in mean and turbulent quantities under skew, while profiles still collapsed under similarity scaling and maintained near-Gaussian stress shapes.
watch_item: The findings come from a controlled laboratory setup, so the observed invariance may not fully extend to more complex 3D flows with stronger geometry, unsteadiness, or higher skew.
paper_title: Effects of mean flow skew on turbulent shear layers. Part II. Experimental investigation
